correctness.rationale: Reconstructed incidence states for graph E={01,12,23,03,04,45}, with twelve vertex-edge primitive pairs, by independent integer-bitmask enumeration. Generalized matching admissibility and ordinary no-directed-cycle admissibility yield exactly 297 versus 287 nonempty faces, f-vectors (12,53,106,94,30,2) and (12,53,106,92,24). A fresh matching/DAG implementation produced 147 and 141 matched pairs and complete oriented Hasse diagrams of 962 and 912 covers, both acyclic, leaving a single critical 0-cell and respectively two and four critical 3-cells. Forman thus proves GM(G)≈∨²S³ and M(G)≈∨⁴S³, not merely homology.

value.rationale: This is the smallest cycle length in the cited single-leaf theorem, extended by the next naturally motivated tail edge. It establishes the first explicit boundary at which generalized and ordinary discrete-Morse complexes separate, with exact unequal sphere multiplicities 2 versus 4. A future comparison theorem needs this precise small counterexample; no family-wide result is asserted or required.

limitations: The discrete-Morse DAG certificate proves these finite homotopy types, not a formula for arbitrary unicyclic graphs.
